clue.text: The special latitude of a king to interrupt a subject

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another thing, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a subject of discussion
R, from Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is granted unusual freedom to break in on one of his subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latitude' looks like freedom or leeway and 'subject' like a royal subject, but one is geography and the other a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are particular named parallels of the globe, unlike ordinary lines of latitude.

clue.text: Confidence in cereal product

indicators.note: a product is something made by working on raw material, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone trusts a breakfast cereal brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance is trust or dependence placed in someone or something, much the same as confidence in them.

clue.text: Shortest point — that's the way

blocks.note: the pith is the essential point of an argument
i.e. stands for id est, that is
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone says the quickest point is the route to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the way' sounds like encouragement; it splits into i.e. and a street.
explanation.definitionFit: The pithiest remark is the most concise and to the point, so the briefest in words.

clue.text: It sounds like a chestnut on old King William

blocks.note: first meaning: a horse chestnut that has won bouts in the schoolyard game of conkers, whose name it closely echoes
second meaning: the title of William I, who won England in 1066

explanation.surface: The name of an old king is said to resemble a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British children's game in which horse chestnuts on strings are swung at each other; a winning nut was once called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: William I is known by this epithet after the Norman invasion, and a victorious conker was also given it.

clue.text: Centre of activity for a company — one with pride

blocks.note: a gang is a group or company of people
a group of lions is called a pride

explanation.surface: A firm's busiest hub, run by someone who takes pride in the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' reads as self-respect, but it is the collective noun for lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides its sense of a nerve cluster, the word is used figuratively for any hub or focus of energy and organisation.

clue.text: Termination of court action on three counts

definitions.text: Termination of court action on three counts

blocks.note: surface reading: a lawsuit ended on three charges
setter's reading: a tennis court, where the final point settles three levels of scoring at once

explanation.surface: A legal case is closed, with three charges dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'counts' suggest law and charges, but the court is for tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The umpire's call at the final point of a tennis match announces it is over on every level of scoring.

clue.text: The habitat of the water-boat-man?

blocks.note: surface reading: where the water boatman insect lives
setter's reading: a man in a boat on the water, the Venetian rower

explanation.surface: A natural history question about where a pond insect lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The water boatman is a pond bug; the hyphens split it into a man who works a boat on Venice's canals.
explanation.definitionFit: The gondolier spends his working life in the Venetian boat he rows, so it is jokingly his home.

clue.text: Note in one column can be copied

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a table is figures set out in columns

explanation.surface: A newspaper item written in one column is reproduced elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' and 'column' read like a journalist's piece, but are a sol-fa note and a table of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imitable can be reproduced or mimicked, so it is capable of being copied.

clue.text: Sort of true Englishman can obviously count a lot

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variety of it, so the letters appear in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
E, the abbreviation for English, followed by man

explanation.surface: A typical honest Englishman is good at counting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Englishman' looks like one word of the anagram; it splits into E for English plus a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A numerate person is competent with numbers and arithmetic, so able to count and calculate well.

clue.text: Sort of blonde, but not brassy!

blocks.note: first meaning: a very pale silvery shade of fair hair
second meaning: a precious metal, as opposed to one made of cheap brass

explanation.surface: A hair colour described as fair but not cheap or garish.
explanation.walkthrough: A brassy blonde is a harsh, cheap-looking dye job; the clue plays that against a shade named after a much more valuable metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A very pale silvery hair colour is called a platinum blonde, after the white precious metal.

clue.text: Hospital dropping a line saying how a patient is?

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so these letters are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: an old name for a hospital
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: A hospital sends a note describing the condition of one of its patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping a line' sounds like writing a letter; here it means removing A and RY from the end of the hospital word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick or frail person in hospital is weak and in poor health, which is the adjective required.

clue.text: The uniform for domestic duties

blocks.note: first meaning: the plain working dress soldiers wear
second meaning: menial chores such as cleaning given to soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone asks what outfit to wear for housework.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army the word covers both the menial chores done around barracks and the drab clothing worn while doing them.

clue.text: Instant thatch? What a yarn!

blocks.note: a mo, short for moment, is an instant
thatch is jocular slang for a head of hair

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a tall story about growing a full head of hair overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a tall tale, which the exclamation encourages, but it means spun thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a thread spun from the silky hair of the Angora goat, used for knitting and weaving.

clue.text: American city girl with a classical dress

blocks.note: a girl's name
the toga was the robe of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A young woman from a US city turns up in an ancient-style gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Saratoga Springs is a town in New York State, famous for its racecourse and a Revolutionary War battle.

clue.text: It's carried by the Colonel of the Life Guards or his staff

definitions.text: the Colonel of the Life Guards

blocks.clueFragment: the Colonel of the Life Guards
blocks.note: first meaning: the court title of this officer
second meaning: the gilded rod he bears at royal ceremonies

explanation.surface: Something carried either by a senior cavalry officer or by his aides.
explanation.walkthrough: The Life Guards are a regiment of the British royal household cavalry. 'Staff' looks like his aides, but means the rod, and the officer is called by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The gilded rod borne at royal ceremonies gives its name to the colonel of the Life Guards who carries it.

clue.text: Dry outback for the Amish, for example

blocks.note: sec is the wine term for dry
read as out back: the back, or final letter, of the word out

explanation.surface: Arid Australian bush land offered to a plain-living American religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outback' reads as the Australian interior, but splits into a word and a position.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a religious group that separated from the Mennonites, and a breakaway religious group is a sect.

clue.text: A devotee of sensual vices in the original bestiary

indicators.note: original means new and inventive, so the letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker described in an old medieval book of beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' seems to mean the first edition of the book; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaris was a Greek city famed for luxury, so a sybarite is a person given over to pleasure and self-indulgence.

clue.text: Pool money first for woollen material

indicators.note: first says the second-named piece goes at the front

blocks.note: cash is money
a mere is a lake or pool

explanation.surface: Clubbing together funds up front to buy wool cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool money' reads as sharing funds; it is a lake and cash, in the opposite order.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is the fine soft wool of the Kashmir goat and the fabric woven from it.

clue.text: Transfer germ when conversing

indicators.note: conversing is talking, so the word is judged by how it is said rather than spelt

blocks.note: a germ is a seed, the starting point of growth

explanation.surface: Passing on an infection by talking to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Germ' suggests disease, but here it means a seed, as in wheat germ.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to hand over territory or rights to someone else, which is a transfer.

clue.text: Puppet man

blocks.note: first meaning: someone wholly controlled by another
second meaning: a living being, a person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Puppet man' reads as a puppeteer; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature can be a person dependent on a patron, a mere tool, and also any living being or human.

clue.text: Hair-do or nail manicure? A stud doesn't need all of this

indicators.note: not all of the phrase is needed, so only a run of its letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run on across the words
surface padding that completes the picture of a beauty salon

explanation.surface: Choosing between a hairstyle and a manicure, with a remark about a stud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manicure' seems an anagram signal but nothing needs rearranging; 'stud' suggests jewellery or a horse, but here it is a large-headed nail.
explanation.definitionFit: Doornails were large-headed studs once hammered into doors for strength and decoration.

clue.text: Perhaps run gala by river, where it's sandy

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible version of the letters, one of their many arrangements

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone suggests holding a fete beside a river where the ground is sandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand is made of small grains, so a sandy texture is grainy, which is the adjective required.

clue.text: Wild birds round the marsh are yellow

indicators.note: round says one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: game is wild birds hunted for sport and food
a bog is a marsh

explanation.surface: Wild birds flying over a marsh look yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a gum resin from Cambodia giving a deep golden pigment, and the name is used for that colour.

clue.text: Reception is available to callers

blocks.note: first meaning: a social gathering held in one's own house
second meaning: in and receiving visitors

explanation.surface: A front desk tells visitors someone is free to see them.
explanation.definitionFit: An at-home is a party for guests in the host's house, and someone in their house can receive visitors.

clue.text: Indiscriminate land measure causing widespread loss

blocks.note: mass as an adjective means on a large scale, affecting everyone without distinction
an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: A careless way of measuring land leads to people losing large amounts of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land measure' looks like one idea about property; it is the unit alone, and 'widespread loss' is loss of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the slaughter of many people, or in sport a crushing defeat, so a great loss on a wide scale.

clue.text: Where to make cold buffet

blocks.note: to ice something is to chill it
to buffet is to strike, as boxers do

explanation.surface: A question about where a cold buffet should be prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a spread of food, but it is the verb meaning to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a refrigerator or chilled cabinet, the place where food is kept and chilled.

clue.text: Judicial authority recalled point in hearing

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read back to front
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the nub is the central point of a matter
a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A court remembers a point made during a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' and 'hearing' both sound like court business; only 'Judicial authority' is the definition, and a nub is the central point of a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body set up to judge disputes, such as an employment tribunal, so it is a court with legal power.

clue.text: Canines offered as gifts by desperate people

definitions.text: offered as gifts by desperate people
definitions.note: a cryptic description rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: the pointed teeth below the eyes

blocks.clueFragment: offered as gifts by desperate people
blocks.note: second meaning: from the idiom about giving these for something you want badly

explanation.surface: Pets handed over as presents by people at the end of their tether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canines' suggests dogs. Someone who would give their eye-teeth for something wants it desperately.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper canine teeth sit directly below the eyes, hence the name for these pointed teeth.

clue.text: Name inscribed in ships' bows

indicators.note: something inscribed in an object is written into it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: keel is a poetic word for a ship
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A name painted on the front of some vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bows' looks like the front of the ships, but it is the verb: bends at the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneel is to go down on one knee, a kind of bow in reverence or submission.
